title: Implementation of nonlocal multi-photon interference by mode swapping
authors: Holger F. Hofmann, Yuki Kodama, Jonte R. Hance
abstract: Multi-photon interference can be observed using independently generated photons as input. In the most simple case, these photons meet up at a beam splitter, resulting in quantum interference between transmission and reflection of the photons. Here, we show that non-local multi-photon interference can be implemented by using a mode swap operation to generate entanglement between the photons detected in the outputs of two spatially separated interferometers. The spatial separation of the output photons makes this implementation of multi-photon interference particularly suitable for quantum protocols that distribute quantum information to different parties.
summary: This paper shows how to achieve non-local multi-photon interference by implementing a mode swap operation between two separate interferometers. By generating entanglement across these separated locations, the authors demonstrate a non-local Hong-Ou-Mandel effect. This technique is particularly valuable for quantum protocols that require distributing quantum information to distant parties.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of implementing and understanding non-local multi-photon interference in quantum optical systems.
main_result: It demonstrates that a mode swap operation can generate entanglement between photons in two spatially separated interferometers, thus realizing a non-local Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) effect.
method: The method involves modeling the system using optical qubits and employing a mode swap operation followed by post-selection to project the state onto a maximally entangled subspace.
model_or_system: The physical system is based on optical quantum information using multi-photon interference across two spatially separated interferometers (System A and System B). The analysis uses a four-mode photon number basis to model the state evolution.
key_observables: The key observable is the non-local correlation of photon detections, confirming the non-local HOM effect.
important_parameters: The analysis is concerned with the coherence properties across spatially separated modes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on post-selection ($\hat{\Pi}$) to restrict the outcomes to the desired qubit subspace.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the basic mode swapping circuit, showing the paths forming the local systems A and B.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general importance of multi-photon interference to defining the system using local multi-mode setups, demonstrating how the mode swap generates entanglement, and finally using this entanglement to prove the non-local HOM effect.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant for quantum optics and quantum information, as it provides a concrete mechanism (mode swapping) to engineer non-local quantum correlations essential for quantum networking and distributed quantum computation.
